author: Abigale Racine
title: Manistee County commissioners approve pay increases, IT upgrades - NewsBreak
text:
By Abigale Racine ,
12 hours ago Manistee County government meetings take place at 415 Third St., in Manistee. (Manistee News Advocate/File Photo) MANISTEE COUNTY — Employee raises, computer replacements and a new technology reserve were the most recent actions taken by the Manistee County Board of Commissioners .
The public can attend board meetings virtually on Zoom or in person at the Manistee County Courthouse and Government Center, located at 415 Third St. in Manistee.
The next meeting will be at 5 p.m. Sept. 15. The meeting will also serve as a public hearing for Manistee County's 2026-27 budget .
Here are key takeaways from the August meeting:
Staff raises Initially, commissioners discussed a 3% wage increase for non-union county workers, court staff and elected officials for the 2026-27 fiscal year.
The board then discussed whether a 3.5% raise was possible.
To make the half-percentage point increase possible, departments were asked to identify $1,000 in savings within their budgets.
Officials said departments found savings and shifted some expenses to contingency funds, allowing the county to offer the larger raise while projecting a budget deficit of about $354,675.
The board unanimously approved the 3.5% increase.
In June, the board voted to switch to a self-funded health insurance plan for county employees and their dependents, a decision expected to save the county $85,000 annually while avoiding an 8% renewal increase employees otherwise would have faced under the current plan.
The switchover will become effective Oct. 1.
Computer purchases Commissioners approved a $64,982.46 purchase from Insight Enterprises to replace aging county computers.
County IT director Gordan McLellan presented two quotes, from Insight Enterprises and ProVantage, for the county’s annual computer replacement cycle. Typically for purchases, three bids are presented to the board.
McLellan said that market constraints, including rapidly changing computer prices and quote windows, are difficult to follow within the board's normal bidding timeline.
He added that both bids involved identical systems and warranty packages, and that he recommended the Insight Enterprises bid.
Aged-out desktops and laptops are either recycled or reused elsewhere for county operations.
Tech contingency fund Commissioners voted to change what happens to unused funds left in individual county departments' contingency accounts.
The board voted to have 25% of leftover department funds contribute toward building a pool designated for technological needs and upgrades; the remaining 75% will continue going to the county's contingency fund.
A government contingency account allows an agency to cover expenses not included in the county's regular budget, acting as a financial safety net for unexpected items.
The revised policy also increased the amount that departments can spend from their contingency funds without first seeking board approval; however, the new spending limit was not defined during the meeting.
summary: To make the half-percentage point increase possible, departments were asked to identify $1,000 in savings within their budgets. Officials said departments found savings and shifted some expenses to contingency funds, allowing the county to offer the larger raise while projecting a budget deficit of about $354,675. In June, the board voted to switch to a self-funded health insurance plan for county employees and their dependents, a decision expected to save the county $85,000 annually while avoiding an 8% renewal increase employees otherwise would have faced under the current plan.
